results.term_definition:
Moons are celestial bodies that orbit planets, dwarf planets, or smaller objects such as asteroids. The Earth has one moon, called the Moon. Most other Solar System planets have moons, although Mercury and Venus do not. The dwarf planet Pluto has several moons as do a small number of other dwarf planets and asteroids. Moons are natural satellites; artificial satellites such as those used for communication or scientific purposes are not moons. 

Many moons formed in orbit around the planet, dwarf planet, or other body that they orbit. It is thought that the Moon formed orbiting the Earth from material ejected from a major collision between the Earth and a planetoid in an early stage of the Solar System's formation. Many other (mostly smaller) moons are asteroids which were captured by the gravity of the object they orbit.
